features.name: CameraVideoStabilization
features.note: UWP golden renders a gray preview with two visible buttons (VS toggle + record), both disabled because no camera is attached on this machine. The migrated WinUI 3 app renders a FULLY BLANK/white content area in two independent captures: the StatusText fallback (present in the UIA tree with full text) is not visually rendered, and both buttons are pushed to x=1248 in a 1280-wide window so they are clipped at the right edge and effectively invisible. Per the parity rubric a blank-rendering scenario is a fail. Core feature (camera preview, VS toggle, recording) was also deferred to empty no-op Click handlers with both buttons IsEnabled=False; this matches the UWP's disabled state on a camera-less machine, so it is not a NEW behavioral regression (behavioral_regressions=0), but no feature behavior was preserved and the substitute fallback UI does not display. Structural Compare-Parity reported PASS only because the source-derived checklist had 0 controls (Extract-UwpFeatureChecklist did not parse MainPage.xaml, which lives in the shared/ sibling folder); that gate is not meaningful here, so this verdict rests on the screenshot comparison and UIA evidence.
